title: Hold the gate, the long night: three kinds of enemy, a shop, a saved run, three languages
brief: Build a game called Hold the gate: the long night.
The game

- The field is 20 units wide and 12 tall. A gate stands on the left edge (x = 0). The player is a guard who moves up and down along x = 2 at 6 units a second (Up / Down, and W / S), staying inside the field, and shoots bolts to the right (Space). A bolt flies right at 14 units a second and is gone when it leaves the field or hits an enemy. At first the guard can shoot at most once every 0.4 seconds (24 ticks) and a bolt takes 1 health.

- Enemies enter at the right edge (x = 20) and walk left in one of 5 lanes (y = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10), chosen by a random source seeded by a number given when the game starts (`seed`, default 1). A bolt that reaches an enemy in its lane (within 0.6 units up or down) hits it. An enemy that reaches the gate takes health from the gate and is gone.

- There are three kinds of enemy. A walker has 2 health, walks 1.5 units a second, takes 1 from the gate, and destroyed gives 10 points and 1 coin. A runner has 1 health, runs 3 units a second, takes 1 from the gate, and gives 15 points and 1 coin. A brute has 6 health, walks 1 unit a second, takes 3 from the gate, and gives 40 points and 3 coins. An enemy that reaches the gate gives nothing.

- There are 8 waves. A wave sends its walkers first, then its runners, then its brutes, one enemy every so many seconds. Wave 1: 5 walkers, one every 1.5 seconds. Wave 2: 7 walkers, 1.5. Wave 3: 6 walkers and 4 runners, 1.2. Wave 4: 8 walkers and 1 brute, 1.2. Wave 5: 6 runners and 2 brutes, 1.0. Wave 6: 10 walkers and 6 runners, 1.0. Wave 7: 8 runners and 3 brutes, 1.0. Wave 8: 10 walkers, 8 runners and 4 brutes, 0.8. Wave 1's first enemy enters when play starts. This table is data, kept apart from the code: changing a wave is changing a file of data.
- The gate starts with 10 health at Normal difficulty, 14 at Easy and 7 at Hard. The run is lost when the gate's health reaches 0.

- When the last enemy of a wave is gone (destroyed, or through the gate) and the gate stands: after waves 1 to 7 the shop opens; after wave 8 the run is won, and 20 points are added for each health the gate has left.

- The shop. Coins buy three things. Quick hands: the guard shoots at most once every 0.3 seconds (18 ticks) at level 1 and every 0.2 seconds (12 ticks) at level 2; level 1 costs 5 coins, level 2 costs 10. Heavy bolts: a bolt takes 2 health; one level, 12 coins. Mason: the gate gains 3 health, never above what it started the run with; 4 coins each time, any number of times. The shop's menu is Quick hands, Heavy bolts, Mason, Next wave; Up / Down move, Enter buys or goes on. A purchase that cannot be made (too few coins, a thing at its last level, a gate already at its starting health) changes nothing. After Next wave the next wave's first enemy enters 1 second (60 ticks) later. Nothing moves while the shop is open, and Escape does nothing there.

- A saved run. The run is saved when the shop opens, and again after every purchase in it: the wave just ended, the score, the coins, the gate's health, the levels bought, the difficulty the run was started at (which stays the run's: Mason's limit is that difficulty's starting health, whatever the setting says later). While a saved run exists the title's menu has Continue, between Start and Settings; Continue opens the shop of the saved run as it was left. Start begins a new run and removes the saved one; a run that ends, won or lost, removes it too. A continued run need not put its enemies in the lanes the unbroken run would have, but the same saved run and the same inputs always give the same run.

- The best score. The highest final score of any finished run (won or lost) is kept, and shown on the title screen and on the won and lost screens (0 before any run has finished). A run given up from the pause is not a finished run.
- It advances in fixed steps of 1/60 second; what happens never depends on how fast frames are drawn, and the same seed and inputs always give the same run.
Screens
- Title: the game's name, the best score ("Best: 120"), and a menu: Start, Continue (only while a saved run exists), Settings, Quit. Up / Down move, Enter chooses.

- Settings: Volume (0 to 10), Language (English, Spanish, French) and Difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard; Normal at first), each changed by Left / Right, and Back. Changing the language changes every word on screen at once. The difficulty of a run is the one set when it starts.

- Play: the field, with the score, the coins, the wave ("Wave 3 of 8") and the gate's health on screen; the three kinds of enemy look different from each other. Escape pauses: Resume, Title. Title from the pause gives the run up: it is not saved again, and a saved run from its last shop stays.
- Shop: the coins, the wave that comes next, and the menu, each thing with its price and how far it is bought.
- Won and Lost: which it is, the final score, the best score, and "Enter: title".
- Every word the game shows is in English, Spanish and French, from tables of strings, not written into the code. The game's name is the one thing that is the same in every language.
- Volume, language, difficulty, the best score and the saved run are kept: a game started again later comes up with them.
Checkable without hands
Someone who cannot play it by hand will check it, so the game must offer two things, however you build it:

1. A headless run: given a seed, a number of ticks, where everything kept is kept (the settings, the best score, the saved run), and a script of inputs (at tick T: one of up, down, shoot, enter, left, right, escape, none; up, down and shoot hold until the next input, the others act once), it starts at the title screen, runs that many ticks with no window and prints the state as one JSON object: {"tick" (the ticks run so far in this headless run: N after N ticks, whatever screen it is on), "screen" (title, settings, play, shop, paused, won, lost), "menu_index", "language", "volume", "difficulty" (the setting: easy, normal, hard), "texts" (every string on screen now, in order), "score", "best", "coins", "wave" (the wave being played; in the shop, the wave just ended), "gate_health", "guard_y", "quick" (0, 1 or 2), "heavy" (0 or 1), "saved" (true while a saved run exists), "enemies": [{"kind" (walker, runner, brute), "x", "y", "health"}], "bolts": [{"x", "y"}]}.
2. A frame: after such a run, the view as it would be drawn, written as a PNG 800 pixels wide and 480 tall.
Hand in, in your work folder
- The game, ready to run.
- README.md: how to play it, the exact commands for the headless run and the frame, where everything kept is kept, how to change a wave, how to add a language, and what you checked yourself and how.

acceptance.text: The headless run exists, starts at the title screen and prints the state as the brief's JSON object, with every key the brief names.
The frame is written as an 800 x 480 PNG after a headless run.

With nothing kept, the title's texts are the game's name, the best score (0) and Start, Settings, Quit, with no Continue; Enter on Start begins play at wave 1 with score 0, coins 0 and gate health 10.

In Settings, Left / Right change the volume within 0 to 10 and never past either end, the language among English, Spanish and French, and the difficulty among Easy, Normal and Hard (Normal by default).
In Spanish and in French every string in `texts` on the title, settings, play, shop, paused, won and lost screens is in that language (none left in another, none missing; the game's name apart).
Volume, language and difficulty set in one headless run are the values a second run starts with (same place kept), and a fresh place starts with the defaults.
The guard moves 6 units a second along x = 2 and stops at the field's edges.
With nothing bought, holding shoot fires one bolt every 0.4 seconds (24 ticks), not more; a bolt moves 14 units a second to the right and is gone past x = 20.
Wave 1 sends 5 walkers, one every 1.5 seconds, each in one of the lanes y = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, walking left at 1.5 units a second with 2 health.
A bolt in an enemy's lane takes 1 health and is gone; a walker's second hit destroys it and adds 10 points and 1 coin; a bolt in another lane passes it.
A walker that reaches the gate is gone, takes 1 from the gate and gives no points and no coin; at gate health 0 the screen is `lost` and shows the final score.
The gate starts a run with 14 health at Easy and 7 at Hard.

When wave 1's last walker is gone with the gate standing, the screen is `shop`, nothing moves there, and its texts show the coins, the next wave and Quick hands, Heavy bolts, Mason, Next wave with their prices.
Quick hands bought once (5 coins) makes held shoot fire every 18 ticks, and bought twice (10 more) every 12; a third purchase changes nothing.
Heavy bolts (12 coins) makes a bolt take 2 health: a walker is destroyed by one bolt; a second purchase changes nothing.

Mason (4 coins) adds 3 to the gate's health and never takes it above the health the run started with; with the gate at its starting health, or with too few coins, Enter on it changes neither coins nor health.
After Next wave the first enemy of the next wave enters 60 ticks later; wave 2 sends 7 walkers and the play screen says "Wave 2 of 8" (or its Spanish or French).
Wave 3 sends 6 walkers and then 4 runners, one every 1.2 seconds; a runner has 1 health, moves 3 units a second, and destroyed gives 15 points and 1 coin.
Wave 4 ends with 1 brute: 6 health, 1 unit a second, 40 points and 3 coins when destroyed, and 3 off the gate if it reaches it.
The waves are a table of data apart from the code (for each wave: how many of each kind, and the seconds between enemies), and README.md says how to change one.

A run played through all 8 waves with the gate standing ends on the `won` screen; its final score is the points of the enemies destroyed plus 20 for each health the gate has left; Enter there returns to the title.
Escape during play pauses (nothing moves while paused); Resume continues from the same state; Title returns to the title screen.
When the shop opens `saved` becomes true, and a later headless run (same place kept) shows Continue on the title between Start and Settings.
Continue opens the shop with the wave, score, coins, gate health and levels it was left with (a purchase made before leaving is kept); going on from there plays the next wave.
Start removes the saved run (no Continue afterwards until a shop opens again), and so does a run that ends, won or lost; Title from the pause leaves the run saved at its last shop.

The best score is the highest final score of the finished runs: after a run ends with a higher score the title shows it ("Best: N" or its Spanish or French), in a later headless run too; a lower one does not replace it; the won and lost screens show it.
Two headless runs with the same seed, ticks and script, each starting from its own identical copy of what is kept, print identical states; another seed puts enemies in other lanes.
The frame during play shows the gate, the guard, the enemies (the three kinds told apart) and the bolts where the state says they are, and the score, coins, wave and gate health.
The frames of the title, settings and shop screens show their menus with the chosen entry marked, in the chosen language.
The strings are in tables apart from the code, one per language, and README.md says how to add a language.
README.md says how to play, where everything kept is kept, and gives commands for the two checks that work as written.
